findings.text: follow-on: the judge question's `forbidden`/`canonical` options do not reuse the smoke read's calibrated Choice — the brief's 'reuse its question and options' — and instead hand the model the registry's `forbidden_variants` (regex patterns such as '\$\$[^$]*(dl_p/B_p|dl/B)[^$]*\$\$' and 'the separatrix') as literal written forms; the recorded live run over-fired plasma_boundary as forbidden for all four fixtures, including the beryllium and electron entries whose boundary is the last closed flux surface, where the smoke read's boundary gloss Choice was correct on all four. Report-only, so nothing is capped; recorded here as a candidate measurement before the check leaves report-only.

follow-on: the judge stage is gated on `not state.skip_audit`, so `--skip-audit` silently disables the Jev-backed judgement too, though plan 7 and the brief describe it as a stage of its own beside the audit stage; a user skipping only the deterministic Layer 1 audits also loses the judge, and no test exercises the skip_audit=true branch.

follow-on: the live run is evidenced only by the fragment's prose table (8 calls, USD 0.000321, per-fixture answers); no driver script or raw decisions log is committed beside it and no live-run log is listed in test_logs, so the calls/answers/cost cannot be re-derived, unlike the referenced flux-surface-average smoke read which ships its script beside it.
